_comment: How Moroccan Arabic (the urban koine of Casablanca and Rabat) says the letters a romanisation of standard Arabic writes, for lib/translit.py: read before lib/lang/ar.ipa.json for a book or a video written in Moroccan (variety ar.mor). Whatever this file does not say is ar.ipa.json's. ONLY the consonant correspondences every description gives and the Moroccan dictionary agrees with; ق is kept as q (the cities say q). The case endings go (`from_standard.pausal`, the rule in ar.ipa.json: kataba > katab). The other vowels are NOT touched: Moroccan drops most of standard Arabic's short vowels (kataba > kteb), and where and how is the research brief's, so a standard word keeps its standard vowels here.
_sources: Richard S. Harrell, A Short Reference Grammar of Moroccan Arabic (Georgetown University Press, 1962), ch. 1: the interdentals > stops t d ḍ, q kept in the cities, ج said ž.
Dominique Caubet, L'arabe marocain, vol. 1 (Peeters, 1993): the same.
Jeffrey Heath, Jewish and Muslim Dialects of Moroccan Arabic (RoutledgeCurzon, 2002): the regional q/g split, which is why q is left as it is.

from_standard._map: A letter of the standard romanisation (the standard dictionary's hits, shown in a text written in Moroccan) to the letter the cities say: ث ذ ظ are t d ḍ (ṯalāṯa > talāta, ḏahab > dahab, ẓahr > ḍahr). ج is LEFT j: Moroccan says it ž, but the Moroccan dictionary writes it j (142 of its 151 entries with ج), so one sound keeps one letter in the panel. Left out, to the research brief: the short vowels, ق as g in the countryside, ž > z beside another sibilant (zūž).
